entities.summary: August Friedrich Ferdinand Graf von der Goltz was a key figure in the early modern period, serving as Minister for Foreign Affairs of Prussia between 1808 and 1814. He was the first person to hold this title, marking a significant shift in Prussia's diplomatic leadership. Von der Goltz's tenure was marked by the Napoleonic Wars, during which he navigated the complex web of alliances and rivalries between European powers. His diplomatic efforts played a crucial role in Prussia's survival during this tumultuous period. The Treaty of Schönbrunn, signed in 1815, marked the end of the war and cemented Prussia's position as a major power in Europe. Von der Goltz's legacy extended beyond his own lifetime, as his diplomatic tactics influenced generations of Prussian leaders. His commitment to maintaining Prussia's independence and territorial integrity set a precedent for future generations of German politicians. Today, von der Goltz is remembered as a skilled diplomat who deftly navigated the treacherous landscape of European politics during a time of great upheaval.
